prisoner.name: Roger Aarons
prisoner.description: Roger Aarons was a New York pacifist associated with the Committee for Nonviolent Action. He participated in its protest against the Polaris submarine program and was prosecuted after the World Citizen entered the restricted launch area in November 1960.

case.charges: Knowingly violating a Coast Guard restricted-zone order at the Ethan Allen launching; 50 U.S.C. 192.
case.prosecutor: John P. Diuguid; Hadley W. Austin
case.sentence: One year, suspended after 90 days, followed by five years of probation. His conviction was affirmed on October 30, 1962. Contemporary reporting confirms detention at New Haven from the November 22 arrest through at least November 26, 1960. The full time actually served and custody endpoints remain unverified.

prisoner.name: Victor Richman
prisoner.description: Victor Richman was a Columbia University student and anti-nuclear activist prosecuted with other Committee for Nonviolent Action participants after the November 1960 Ethan Allen protest. Contemporary reports document his imprisonment at New Haven and subsequently at Danbury.

case.charges: Knowingly violating a Coast Guard restricted-zone order at the Ethan Allen launching; 50 U.S.C. 192.
case.prosecutor: John P. Diuguid; Hadley W. Austin
case.sentence: One year, with 90 days to serve and the balance suspended. He remained in New Haven custody several days after the November 22, 1960 arrest. An August 1961 report describes his confinement at Danbury, including four days in solitary before a fast. His complete custody span and final release date are unverified.

case_updates.name: Bill Henry
case_updates.expected_charges: Trespassing — boarding the Polaris submarine Ethan Allen in protest
case_updates.expected_sentence: One year. He is documented as having served a year at the federal prison in Danbury, Connecticut; his exact admission and release dates are not located, so no custody span is entered.
case_updates.append_sentence: On February 24, 1961, Judge Robert P. Anderson offered release if Henry gave a written pledge against further such actions; Henry refused. CNVA later connected his year at Danbury with both the November 22, 1960 Ethan Allen boarding and the January 28, 1961 George Washington boarding, when the World Citizen was seized. An August 1961 report describes two one-year terms served concurrently, not consecutively.

case_updates.name: Donald Martin
case_updates.expected_charges: Trespassing — boarding the Polaris submarine Ethan Allen in protest
case_updates.expected_sentence: An indefinite youth-offender sentence that could have held him for as long as four years. He refused bail and was held at Danbury awaiting trial by February 1961. His exact release date is unresolved, so no release is entered.

fill.prosecutor: John P. Diuguid; Hadley W. Austin

case_updates.append_sentence: Martin was sentenced as a youth offender on June 19, 1961. By September 1962, reporting placed him in the federal prison at Ashland, Kentucky, after more than a year in custody, and described refusal of parole. The Youth Corrections Act distinguished a four-year limit before conditional release from six years before unconditional discharge; neither limit proves the time Martin actually served. He was also seized during the January 28, 1961 World Citizen action. His final release date remains unverified.

case_updates.name: Richard Zink
case_updates.expected_charges: Interfering with naval vessels — antinuclear Polaris-submarine protest
case_updates.expected_sentence: A federal judge ordered him in June 1961 to serve thirty days of a six-month term — a definite custodial sentence, but no jail register, admission date or release notice proving his exact custody dates has been located, so none is entered.

fill.prosecutor: John P. Diuguid; Hadley W. Austin

case_updates.append_sentence: The sentencing date was June 19, 1961. Zink was named in the federal indictment arising from the November 22, 1960 Ethan Allen restricted-zone protest. An individual admission or release record has not been located.
